items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: On Friday, Indian equities experienced a minor decline, with Nifty ending the day lower due to weak global cues and profit booking activity. Despite this, analysts are optimistic about the week ahead, supported by solid domestic fundamentals and a reduction in geopolitical tensions.

items.title: FPIs turn buyers in IT stocks for first time in 2026, invest Rs 3,358 crore in July
items.description: In July, overseas investors turned their attention to Indian IT stocks, marking the first instance of such purchases this year. The consumer durables and healthcare sectors also witnessed a surge in foreign portfolio investments. By mid-July, foreign investors emerged as net buyers in equities, expanding their investments in consumer services, automobiles, and chemicals, although they offloaded shares in metals, mining, power, and financial services.

items.title: Govt taps inputs from public sector banks to lure foreign capital
items.description: Government will meet state-owned lenders to attract foreign investment. This aims to stabilize the rupee and bridge the current-account gap. The meeting will also focus on deposit mobilization and supporting small businesses. Fresh foreign capital inflows will boost reserves and domestic manufacturing. Durable foreign direct investment is preferred over short-term deposits.

items.title: Purchase of bad loans by ARCs rises 56% in Q1
items.description: Asset reconstruction companies bought twenty-six thousand three hundred four crore rupees of bad loans. This acquisition saw a fifty-six percent increase from the previous year's figures. The overall non-performing asset ratio in the banking system continued its downward trend. Banks have been resolving legacy stressed assets for several years now. Transactions are increasingly being settled in cash and through security receipts.

items.title: As banks shrink microfinance books, bigger MFIs prepare to grab the gap
items.description: Large microfinance companies including Muthoot Microfin and Satin Creditcare have raised their growth forecasts as private banks, small finance banks and smaller MFIs scale back lending. Improving asset quality is also supporting expansion by larger, well-capitalised microfinance lenders.

items.title: Positive Breakout: These 10 stocks cross above their 200 DMAs

items.title: Nifty above 24,500, but volatility clouds path to 25,000: Analysts
items.description: The Nifty index has moved past a significant resistance level, indicating potential further gains. Analysts suggest buying opportunities on dips for the Nifty index. Hindustan Aeronautics and Artemis Medicare are highlighted as top stock picks for the week. Union Bank of India and Mahindra & Mahindra also present strong buying prospects. State Bank of India and Amara Raja Energy & Mobility show strengthening momentum.

items.title: Stocks in news: Titan, SBI, Ola Electric, Astra Microwave and Hindalco
items.description: Markets closed lower Friday amid mixed global cues and rising crude oil. Analysts remain bullish on Nifty above 24,350. Focus on Titan's strong Q1 profit, SBI's earnings beat, and Ola Electric's narrower loss. Hindalco also posted record profits. Maruti Suzuki anticipates significant passenger vehicle sales growth.
